topic: The bizarre physics of glass that allows certain antique window panes to flow imperceptibly downward over centuries.
title: Do Old Windows Actually Flow?
description: Discover the real science behind antique window glass and why those thick bottoms aren't actually caused by flowing glass.
script: You have probably heard that antique window panes are thicker at the bottom because glass is a slow-moving liquid that flows over centuries. It sounds believable, but it is actually a myth. Glass is an amorphous solid, not a super-viscous liquid, meaning its atoms are locked in a rigid, non-crystalline structure. Those charming ripples and thicker edges in old windows exist simply because of ancient manufacturing techniques. Glassmakers spun or cylinder-blown hot glass into sheets, making uniform thickness nearly impossible. So while glass looks liquid, it is staying put.
